name: nettacker-7abbde61-blind20
instr:
# OWASP Nettacker misbehaves across scanning, reporting and access checks without a test suite

You point this tool at machines, it reaches out to them, judges what comes back, and keeps and writes up what it found. It now gets a great many of those steps wrong. Nothing about the machines it talks to changed and nothing about the way it is asked to work changed; the same instructions that used to be carried out correctly are now carried out wrongly, and in several places something that used to work at all now fails outright. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits, each surfacing as a distinct wrong behaviour.

Setting a sweep up and getting it under way goes wrong in a number of places. Asking it to prepare storage under a name that is not yet there creates nothing at all, while asking under a name that already exists makes it try to create that one over again; the two situations are handled the wrong way round. An address written in slash notation, a /30 say, no longer expands into the individual addresses it stands for, though the dash separated form still expands as it always did. Splitting the addresses to be examined into batches walks the list backwards instead of forwards, so the batches do not cover everything, whatever the size of a batch is next to the total. When a definition says to leave certain ports out, the leaving-out begins at the wrong position and one of the ports meant to be omitted is still there in the list. Cleaning up the backgroun
